GAZE: her eyes rest on what she holds.

Her eyes are naturally open and clear, not heavy-lidded or half-closed; brows relaxed and even, neither raised on one side nor furrowed; lips softly closed or only just parted.

Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera exactly as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same. No default card pose, no default front-facing portrait.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus. No logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No readable text or numbers. Any animal or creature that belongs to the place stays separate from her at its own natural scale — never touching, held by or merged with her body.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, never a smaller head or a longer neck. The neck is a natural length and the head sits close to the shoulders. No body-part enlargement, no extra limbs.

FIGURE: keep her exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.
